transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I've been having some trouble with how much I'm eating lately. 

On these late work nights, I’ll order what I tell myself is just going to be dinner, but... it always turns into a whole entrée, plus sides, a dessert, and then I'll even grab extra snacks from my kitchen on top of that. It's just way, way more food than I would ever eat if someone were actually sitting across from me.
After eating this way, do you ever try to compensate or prevent weight gain by making yourself vomit?
No, I don't do anything like that. I just... I just feel really full and uncomfortable afterward, but I don't try to throw up or anything.
During these episodes, do you feel unable to stop eating or control how much you eat?

Yes, definitely. Um, once I start, there’s this point where I’m almost just watching myself keep going. Like, I'll be opening another package, and in my head I'm thinking that I really should stop, but... it just feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands. I just can't seem to stop it.
How often do these episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food occur?

Well, I actually looked back at my delivery receipts and my work calendar recently to see... and it's usually at least once a week. Sometimes it's more than that, depending on how late I'm working, but it's been happening like this for several months now.
How much distress or emotional upset do these eating episodes cause you?

I'm not exactly sure how to measure it, to be honest. Um... it definitely upsets me. I usually just feel really guilty and frustrated with myself after it happens, but I don't really know how to quantify how much distress it causes overall.
How significantly do these episodes distress you—for example, do they cause substantial emotional suffering or interfere with your daily life?

I guess I don't really know how to answer that. I mean, I don't think it stops me from doing my job or going about my day, so it doesn't really interfere like that. It's mostly just what I mentioned—feeling really awful and guilty afterward. I don't know if that counts as substantial suffering, but it definitely bothers me a lot. I just don't have a good way to measure it beyond that.
Would you describe the distress after these episodes as significant or marked emotional suffering, beyond ordinary guilt or regret about overeating?

I honestly don't know how to compare it. Um... I mean, I feel really terrible about it, but I don't know if it crosses the line into marked suffering or if it's just normal regret for eating too much. It just feels like a really heavy, awful guilt. I don't really have a better way to describe it than what I've already said, to be honest. I'm just not sure how to label it.
Would you say the guilt and distress after these episodes is severe and persistent enough that it significantly troubles you, beyond ordinary regret about overeating?

I... I really don't know how else to say it. I've told you how it feels—it's a heavy, awful guilt that bothers me a lot. I just don't know what you mean by "severe and persistent enough" or "beyond ordinary regret." I'm not a doctor, so I can't tell you if it meets whatever specific criteria you're looking for. I just know it makes me feel terrible.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 means no distress and 10 means extreme distress, how distressed do you typically feel because of these eating episodes?

I honestly don't know how to put a number on it. Um... if 10 is the worst thing imaginable, I don't know where my guilt falls on that scale. Like I've been saying, it's just a really bad feeling. I can't really give you an exact rating, I just know it bothers me a lot.
Have you changed your behavior—such as hiding the eating, avoiding other people, or avoiding activities—because of these episodes?

Yeah, I definitely hide it. When I'm around other people, like my coworkers or friends, I'm really careful to just eat a normal or even small amount. But when I'm alone in my condo, usually after midnight, that's when it happens. I actually close the blinds, and I make sure to get rid of all the delivery containers really fast. I just... I'd be completely mortified if anyone ever saw how much food was actually there. So, yes, I go out of my way to make sure no one sees it.
Do you feel significant shame or distress about these episodes even when they do not interfere with your work or other responsibilities?

Um, yeah, I do. I mean, it doesn't really interfere with my work—I still get all my design projects done on time. But the shame is definitely still there. I just feel awful about it regardless of whether I'm keeping up with my everyday responsibilities or not.
